The root cause is that the `revenue` column, despite being a string, is being interpreted as a non-object type (e.g., `string` in pandas with a different dtype) due to how it was read from the CSV, which prevents `str.replace` from working. This happens when pandas infers the dtype as `string` (from `pandas.StringDtype`) instead of `object`. We must explicitly force it to `object` dtype to allow string methods.

We will now re-read the CSV with `dtype` forced for `revenue` to `object` and proceed.
